channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Nate Soares on How AI Really Could Kill Us All
item.description: Since the Hugging Face incident, concerns over AI doomsday scenarios has entered the mainstream. But of course, some people have been warning about this for years, long before LLMs or ChatGPT. In their 2025 book If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies, Nate Soares and Eliezer Yudkowsky spelled out their vision of humanity's inevitable demise once superintelligent AI is built. In this episode, we speak with Soares, who serves as president of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute, about why he believes it's impossible to "align" superintelligent AI, and how exactly the technology can and will go rogue as it gets more and more advanced. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tencent Tells Investors Its $5 Billion Bond Mainly for AI Capex
item.description: Tencent Holdings Ltd. told fixed-income investors Monday that its planned bond offering of about $5 billion will help finance AI-related capital expenditures, people familiar with the matter said, as it doubles down on the sector.
item.dc:creator: Janice Huang

item.title: Firmus IPO Debacle Raises the Bar for Asia AI Deals in Pipeline
item.description: The collapse of Firmus Grid Ltd.’s initial public offering is reverberating through Asia’s booming market for share sales, making investors far pickier about artificial intelligence infrastructure deals that hinge on future earnings.
item.dc:creator: Sangmi Cha

item.title: IMF Chief Alarmed at ‘Slow-Moving Tsunami’ of AI for Jobs, Taxes
item.description: The head of the International Monetary Fund has warned of the disruptive threat from artificial intelligence to the labor market and taxation, urging policymakers to rethink education and act now to help society adapt.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Mirae Asset's CEO on India's AI Advantage
item.description: Mirae Asset's Swarup Mohanty says India is emerging as a compelling non-AI investment hedge globally. He explains how rising capital allocation toward AI-driven productivity could further strengthen India's appeal. He spoke with Menaka Doshi on Bloomberg's Insight with Haslinda Amin. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: IIF CEO on Rising Global Debt
item.description: Institute of International Finance CEO Tim Adams says debt levels in advanced economies will keep rising as governments continue heavy borrowing and the private sector ramps up investment in AI infrastructure. He spoke with Paul Allen on Bloomberg's Insight with Haslinda Amin on the sidelines of the DBS Asia Future Forward Conference. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: TikTok’s Chew and Microsoft’s Althoff Warn About Runaway AI Hype
item.description: The world may be overexcited by the potential of artificial intelligence and overlooking its immaturity, tech leaders warned on Monday, arguing that cybersecurity is a bigger near-term issue than AI developing too quickly.
item.dc:creator: Gao Yuan and Gabrielle Ng

item.title: Beijing Police Launch Probe Into Wealth Manager CreditEase
item.description: Beijing police opened a criminal investigation into companies affiliated with Chinese wealth management firm CreditEase over suspected illegal financial activities.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: IT Distributor Asbis Targets Data Centers and AI to Sustain 476% Stock Rally
item.description: Warsaw-listed electronics distributor Asbis Enterprises Plc is prioritizing sales to data centers and artificial intelligence infrastructure projects to sustain its breakneck stock rally.
item.dc:creator: Konrad Krasuski

item.title: Why the Commodity Bull Market Is Just Beginning
item.description: Adam Rozencwajg, portfolio manager at natural resources firm Goehring and Rozencwajg, joins Merryn Somerset Webb to explain why he thinks the commodity bull market may still be in its early stages. They discuss why gold could fall before reaching new highs, why US shale may have peaked and where he sees opportunities in oil and uranium. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Firmus Fiasco Wipes Out $700 Million of Early Backer Maas’ Value
item.description: Maas Group Holdings Ltd. has lost more than A$1 billion ($699 million) in market value as Firmus Grid Ltd.’s initial public offering unraveled, with the shares extending their decline to a fifth day after Jefferies Financial Group Inc. downgraded its rating.
item.dc:creator: Carmeli Argana

item.title: Dongshan Said to Gauge Demand for Up to $3 Billion Listing
item.description: Printed circuit board maker Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing Co. has started gauging investor interest for a Hong Kong listing that may raise $2 billion to $3 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Julia Fioretti and Sangmi Cha

item.title: Bain’s Bridge Data Centres Seeks to Upsize Loan to $6.6 Billion
item.description: Bain Capital-owned Bridge Data Centres is in talks with banks to more than double the size of an existing loan to about $6.6 billion, people familiar with the matter said, in what would be one of the largest deals for the sector in Asia.
item.dc:creator: Kari Lindberg

item.title: LG's Cho on Latest AI-Powered Forecasting Tools
item.description: Tyger Cho, Director of Business Development and Financial Services at LG AI Research, discusses the the adoption of artificial intelligence in the financial sector and the company's latest AI tool, which forecasts the short-term performance of Korean equity markets. He speaks with Haidi Stroud-Watts on Bloomberg: The Asia Trade. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DBS CEO: Market Repricing Risks on AI Financing
item.description: Tan Su Shan, CEO at DBS Group, says the market is repricing the risks around investments related to the buildup of artificial intelligence that could lead to more discipline in financing. She speaks with Haidi Stroud-Watts from the DBS Asia Future Forward Conference ion Singapore. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DBS CEO Tan Says Market Is Repricing Risks on AI Financing
item.description: The market is repricing the risks around investments related to the buildup of artificial intelligence that could lead to more discipline in financing, according to DBS Group Holdings Ltd. Chief Executive Officer Tan Su Shan.
item.dc:creator: Rthvika Suvarna

item.title: Amazon Is in Talks to Buy AI Startup Decart, WSJ Reports
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. is in negotiations to acquire Decart AI, an artificial intelligence startup, in a deal that could be valued at around $7 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: Xpeng Says It Can Quickly Adapt Car Autopilot Systems for Europe
item.description: Xpeng Inc. can rapidly adapt its advanced driver-assistance technology to European roads using relatively small amounts of data, allowing it to modify its software capabilities for different markets without rebuilding them from scratch.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Is AI Crowding Everyone Else Out of the Bond Market?
item.description: Hyperscalers, data centers and chip companies are borrowing hundreds of billions of dollars to finance the AI buildout, turning the technology boom into one of the biggest new forces in corporate credit. Investors are still buying, but rising concentration, complex data-center financing and competition with government borrowing are raising a harder question: how much AI debt can the market absorb? (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Smart Home Launch Oct. 13 Plans; HomeView Has Mid-November Release
item.description: Fresh details on Apple’s HomeView, HomePod mini and new Apple TV, including release dates, colors, chips and features.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman
